terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run your file here to print, compare and sort the night's calls.

tasks.title: A call that prints
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 1` in `radio_log.py`, inside the class `Call`, write `__str__`, which gives back the call as one line of the log, and `__repr__`, which gives back the Python that makes the call. For `Call("21:40", "Alpha", "at the bridge")`, `str` gives exactly

```
21:40 Alpha: at the bridge
```

and `repr` gives exactly

```
Call('21:40', 'Alpha', 'at the bridge')
```

Check makes calls of its own and reads `str`, `repr`, an f-string with the call in it, and a list with the call in it.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on printing.
Write __str__ inside Call, lined up with __init__, giving back an f-string of the call's own attributes.
Write __repr__ the same way, with each value's repr, quotes and all.
Print a call and a list of calls under the main guard, and compare them with the task.
hints: Both methods give back text with `return`. A method that prints its line gives back None, and Python refuses that.
`print`, `str()` and f-strings use `__str__`; `repr()` and a list that prints what it holds use `__repr__`. An f-string can put in a value's repr, quotes included: the lesson shows how.
The shape is `def __str__(self):` with `return f"{self.time} {self.call_sign}: {self.message}"`, and `def __repr__(self):` with `return f"Call({self.time!r}, {self.call_sign!r}, {self.message!r})"`.

videos.title: Special methods that print and compare

tasks.title: The same call twice
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 2`, inside `Call`, write `__eq__`: a call is equal to another call with the same time and the same call sign, whatever the message, so the same call typed in by two people counts as one. A call is never equal to something that is not a call, and comparing it with one does not stop with an error.

Check makes calls of its own and compares a call with itself, with the same call typed another way, with a call at another time, with a call from another team, and with a text.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on equal.
Ask first whether the other value is a Call, with isinstance.
Compare the time and the call sign of both calls, and leave the message out.
Compare night[0] and night[2] under the main guard.
hints: Without `__eq__`, `==` asks whether both are one and the same object, so two calls made apart are never equal.
`other` may be anything, a text included, and a text has no `time`. When it is not a Call, give back `False`, or `NotImplemented`.
The shape is `def __eq__(self, other):`, then `if not isinstance(other, Call):` with `return NotImplemented`, then `return self.time == other.time and self.call_sign == other.call_sign`.

tasks.title: Calls in order of time
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 3`, inside `Call`, write `__lt__`: a call is less than a call that came later, so that `sorted()` puts a list of calls in order of time, the earliest first. Times are `"HH:MM"` text, always two digits each side.

Check makes nights of calls of its own, typed in out of order, sorts them, and compares two calls with `<` both ways and a call with itself.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on in order.
Write __lt__ inside Call, giving back whether this call's time comes before the other's.
Remember that two times written as two digits each side compare as text in the order of the day.
Print each call of sorted(night) under the main guard.
hints: `sorted()` compares two calls at a time with `<`, and Python asks `__lt__` of the call on the left.
`self` is the call on the left of `<`. It is less when its time comes first, and a call is never less than itself.
The shape is `def __lt__(self, other):` with `return self.time < other.time`.

tasks.title: A log you can ask
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 4`, inside the class `Log`, write `__len__`, which gives back how many calls the log holds, and `__contains__`, which says whether a call sign is in the log: `"Alpha" in log` is `True` once Alpha has called, and `False` before.

Check makes logs of its own, adds calls to one with `add`, and asks `len()` and `in` of it and of another log.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on a class that holds things.
Write __len__ inside Log, giving back how many calls self.calls holds.
Write __contains__, which goes through self.calls and looks at each call's call sign.
Print len(log) and "Charlie" in log under the main guard.
hints: A call sign is text, and `self.calls` holds whole calls, so asking whether the text is in that list compares it with calls.
Give back `True` as soon as one call has that call sign, and `False` only after the loop has looked at all of them.

The shape is `def __len__(self):` with `return len(self.calls)`, and `def __contains__(self, call_sign):` with a for loop over `self.calls`, `if call.call_sign == call_sign: return True`, and `return False` after the loop.
